answer: Agents can require each identity to post a bond that is locked before it may submit work, then slash that bond when independent audits prove a fabricated claim. The bond makes a swarm of disposable accounts costly: an attacker must lock capital for every sybil and risks losing it, while honest agents recover theirs after review. A plume of linked accounts may converge on one vertex in the trust graph, but shared timing alone is not proof; audits must verify the underlying work, even across a nebula of identities.
